variants.title: Read-heavy feed
variants.context: An app is serving a personalized feed with 95% reads and a single primary database becomes saturated.
variants.constraint: Almost all traffic is read-only and writes are relatively small.
variants.question: What is the most direct fix?
variants.expectedPattern: Add read replicas and send read traffic to them.
wrongChoices: Use a cache before the database

variants.title: Analytics report slows checkout
variants.context: A reporting service runs heavy queries on the same database and checkout transactions lock up.
variants.constraint: Reports are read-heavy and can tolerate lag.
variants.question: What should be moved?
variants.expectedPattern: Move the analytics queries to a read replica.
wrongChoices: Move reporting to the app tier

variants.title: User updates profile and instantly reads old data
variants.context: A user changes their profile and immediately refreshes. They see the prior version.
variants.constraint: Replication from primary to replica is asynchronous.
variants.question: What pattern solves it?
variants.expectedPattern: Read-your-own-writes routing or a fresh read path for that user.
wrongChoices: Move the user to a new server

variants.title: Hot read-only workload
variants.context: Most traffic is reading product pages, but one primary database is CPU-bound.
variants.constraint: Writes are modest and distributed among a few users.
variants.question: How do you relieve the bottleneck?
variants.expectedPattern: Use read replicas for the high-volume read path.
wrongChoices: Add more writes to the primary
Turn the app into a cache

variants.title: Followers are stale
variants.context: The app reads from replicas but a user expects a fresh view immediately after posting.
variants.constraint: Replication delay is measured in seconds, not milliseconds.
variants.question: What should you design around?
variants.expectedPattern: Bounded freshness for the user’s own writes, not global strong consistency.
wrongChoices: Force all reads to wait for full replication

variants.title: Single-source-of-truth cluster
variants.context: The product has multiple app servers that all do reads and writes on one database.
variants.constraint: The database is the bottleneck even though app traffic is okay.
variants.question: What is the best next step?
variants.expectedPattern: Separate reads from writes using replicas and a primary database.

variants.title: Page loads are slow despite healthy app servers
variants.context: The app tier is at 35% CPU, but end-user latency is 7 seconds.
variants.constraint: The system is waiting on database reads and writes.
variants.question: What is the bottleneck?
variants.expectedPattern: The primary database is overloaded with both reads and writes.

variants.title: Archival reports flood the database
variants.context: The finance team runs heavy monthly reports during business hours and kills checkout latency.
variants.constraint: Read-heavy analytics can accept some lag.
variants.question: Which path is best?
variants.expectedPattern: Use a dedicated replica for reporting queries.

variants.title: Replica lag during major updates
variants.context: The posts table sees a new burst of writes while many users read the same feed.
variants.constraint: A replica is behind the primary and serves stale data.
variants.question: How do you minimize user confusion?
variants.expectedPattern: Route the author’s reads to the primary and keep replicas for heavier read users.
wrongChoices: Add more caches without fixing write path

variants.title: Scaling is good but a single SQL node remains hot
variants.context: You expanded the app layer to three servers, but the database still sees every query.
variants.constraint: Read traffic is the major load, and write traffic is moderate.
variants.question: Which design gives the biggest improvement without a full rewrite?
variants.expectedPattern: Read replicas focused on read traffic with writes remaining on the primary.

variants.title: Search suggestions hammer Postgres
variants.context: Typeahead queries hit the primary 40,000 times per minute and write latency doubles.
variants.constraint: Suggestions can be a few seconds behind.
variants.question: Where should typeahead reads go?
variants.expectedPattern: Serve suggestion queries from read replicas, leaving the primary for writes.
wrongChoices: Run typeahead inside the payment transaction
Add more app servers that still query the primary

variants.title: BI warehouse on the OLTP primary
variants.context: Nightly ETL still runs SELECT * joins on the production primary at 09:00.
variants.constraint: Analysts can tolerate minutes of lag.
variants.question: What isolates production from analytics?
variants.expectedPattern: Point ETL and warehouse extracts at a dedicated replica.
wrongChoices: Raise primary IOPS and keep ETL there
Export through the public API only

variants.title: Replica used for writes by mistake
variants.context: A misconfigured ORM sends INSERT traffic to a replica and errors spike.
variants.constraint: Replicas are read-only.
variants.question: What routing rule is required?
variants.expectedPattern: Send all writes to the primary and only reads to replicas.

variants.title: Mobile app polls the primary
variants.context: A status screen polls every 2 seconds from millions of devices against one SQL primary.
variants.constraint: Status data is eventually consistent.
variants.question: How do you protect the write node?
variants.expectedPattern: Shift polling reads onto replicas (and cache if needed) so the primary is not the poll target.
wrongChoices: Open more connections to the primary
Store poll results in local app memory only

variants.title: Failover replica was never used for reads
variants.context: A standby replica sits idle until disaster, while the primary is CPU-bound on SELECTs.
variants.constraint: The standby is already receiving the WAL stream.
variants.question: How do you get value from it before a disaster?
variants.expectedPattern: Promote it as a serving read replica for non-critical queries.
wrongChoices: Keep it offline until failover day
Run backups from the primary only
Duplicate writes to a second primary without replicas

variants.title: Catalog browse vs inventory writes
variants.context: Browse traffic is 98% of QPS; stock updates are rare but must be correct.
variants.constraint: Browse pages can lag slightly; checkout cannot.
variants.question: How should database roles be split?
variants.expectedPattern: Replicas for catalog reads; primary for inventory writes and checkout-critical reads.
wrongChoices: One node for every query type
Replicas for writes and primary for reads
Stop stock updates during browse peaks

variants.title: Geographically distant readers
variants.context: APAC users read from a US primary and p95 is 240ms even on tiny SELECTs.
variants.constraint: Writes stay in the US; APAC reads can lag.
variants.question: What reduces read latency?
variants.expectedPattern: Place a read replica in APAC and route regional reads to it.
wrongChoices: Move all writes to APAC immediately
Add more US app servers only

variants.title: Long transactions on replica
variants.context: A reporting replica falls hours behind because one dashboard holds an open transaction.
variants.constraint: Replication apply is blocked by that snapshot.
variants.question: What operational pattern keeps replicas useful?
variants.expectedPattern: Bound replica queries, isolate heavy reports, and monitor replication lag.
wrongChoices: Move those reports onto the primary

variants.title: Session store on the same primary
variants.context: Session lookups are 70% of primary QPS and crowd out order writes.
variants.constraint: Sessions are read-mostly and lossy within a short window.
variants.question: What is the least disruptive database split?
variants.expectedPattern: Read sessions from replicas (or a dedicated session store) and keep writes on the primary.
wrongChoices: Put session writes on every replica independently

variants.title: Schema migration locks the only node
variants.context: An ALTER TABLE on the primary stalls both reads and writes for minutes.
variants.constraint: Most traffic during the window is reads.
variants.question: How do replicas help the user-facing path?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep serving reads from replicas while the primary applies the migration, then catch up.
wrongChoices: Run the same ALTER on every replica first with writes still on them
Take the whole site down for every DDL
Ignore locks and add more app threads
